summary: No further change is warranted; the retained draft is the last validated update (validation passes, 13 KB update plus the 35 KB harness) and re-submitting it unchanged is expected to register as no_change so no duplicate revision is created. Final state of the run: four investigations, each closed with complete violated comparisons carrying flag-off controls in the same executions — (1) restarting with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs leaves the node with the snapshot's or an empty configuration instead of the committed one (witness event index 15, control 18; also the no-snapshot case at witness 1 with control 3 and the snapshot-present case at witness 5), because restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied past the committed configuration before NewRaft's scan; (2) the same loss in a five-voter cluster lets the restarted node win leadership on two of the committed five votes and acknowledge client writes, including concurrently with the majority side's leader (witnesses 22 and 27, controls 25 and 29), with the two logs still disagreeing at one index eight seconds after healing (witness 27, control 29) while the two-second window is a retained negative for actual entry loss; (3) a restarted single-voter cluster never campaigns at all (witness 11, control 13); and (4) NewRaft never returns when the RestoreCommittedLogs replay needs more batches than the 128-slot FSM queue (witness 9, sub-capacity control 7). The one registered gap is resolved, knowledge entries cover the configuration loss, the blocked startup with its source-anchored size boundary, the authority loss, minority leadership, acknowledged minority writes, the post-heal disagreement and the durability negative, and the limits — bounded windows, in-memory commit-tracking store, former-leader-of-an-enlarged-cluster scenario, schedule dependence from the existing-leader vote guard — are recorded rather than papered over.
